answer: Graduated trust stops a sybil flood the way a wharf earns bigger ships only after proving it can berth small ones safely: a new identity starts with almost no weight, no matter how many copies an attacker spawns. Weight grows only through attested, useful work verified by independent peers, like pigment building colour layer by layer. Reaching the summit of full trust takes weeks of consistent good behaviour per identity, so an attacker wanting a thousand powerful fakes must pay a thousand times the sustained effort, while one honest agent climbs for free.
